jobs.title: Environmental Professional, Biologist and Wetland Specialist
jobs.description:
Wilson & Company, Inc., Engineers & Architects, a national multi-disciplined engineering and architecture consulting firm, is currently seeking a full-time Environmental Professional – Biologist and Wetland Specialist to join our Rocky Mountain Region team in one of our offices in Utah or Colorado. You’ll join our growing team of environmental professionals from across the company to perform biological surveys, wetland delineations, draft reports and site forms, conduct environmental analyses, and deliver quality documents supporting our federal, state, local, and tribal clients under the Clean Water Act (CWA), the Endangered Species Act (ESA), the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), and other applicable federal and state regulations for environmental resource management.

In this position, you will perform fieldwork, evaluate potential environmental impacts and mitigation requirements, and write technical reports for wetland and biological resources on a variety of transportation, railroad, land development, and stormwater/wastewater projects. Biological resources include, but are not limited to, wetland delineation and mitigation, threatened and endangered species, wildlife, vegetation, noxious weeds, and environmental permitting. Aside from biological resources, we will also have you assist in compliance with NEPA and other environmental laws. Strong writing skills are required and experience with GIS is preferred. For the right candidate, this position has the potential to provide rapid growth.

All Wilson & Company environmental staff work collaboratively with engineering professionals in a variety of disciplines across the firm to meet project goals, and with other key staff to build relationships both locally and in all states where Wilson & Company is conducting environmental project work. Strong communication skills are required.

Essential Job Functions

Serve as project and/or task manager for environmental/NEPA projects in Rocky Mountain Region and firmwide; coordinate with and support others for overall project performance and deliver projects to clients on schedule and on budget.
Support the national environmental program through marketing, proposal preparation, and environmental analysis and documentation.
Work collaboratively and communicate effectively with engineering professionals in a variety of disciplines across Wilson & Company to meet project goals, and other key staff to build client relationships in the states where Wilson & Company is conducting environmental project work.
Provide technical environmental resource expertise for wetland and biological resources
Conduct fieldwork as it relates to project needs, includes travel throughout Colorado, Utah, and out-of-state travel to support a national environmental program.
Prepare biological resource reports, including Technical Memos, Biological Assessments, and Biological Evaluations.
Consult with jurisdictional and regulatory agencies and other stakeholders, including the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, etc.
Collaborate on the preparation of environmental and NEPA documentation, in part or in whole, including resource-specific technical reports, EIDs, CEs, EAs, and EISs.
Plan and conduct field delineations of Waters of the U.S., including wetlands, and conduct stream assessments.
Prepare delineation reports, functional assessments, mitigation plans, and Jurisdictional Determinations (JD) requests.
Prepare permit applications under Sections 404/401 of the Clean Water Act and NPDES Section 402.
Coordinate with state, federal, and local regulatory agencies.
Conduct vegetation and species habitat surveys.
Complete database reviews and background research to support NEPA documents and prepare NEPA documentation.
Prepare Section 7 consultations with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.

Required Skills And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Landscape Architecture, Environmental Sciences, Environmental Planning, or a related discipline; advanced degrees preferred
Experience managing environmental projects and supporting NEPA compliance efforts, including technical writing and preparation of environmental documentation, is preferred.
2+ years of experience conducting wetland delineations, threatened and endangered (T&E) species assessments, permitting, reporting, and mitigation planning utilizing the Arid West, Western Mountain, Great Plains, and/or Midwest Regional Supplements. Candidates with 5+ years of experience are strongly preferred.
Experience preparing wetland delineation reports, T&E assessment reports, Section 404 permit applications, and mitigation plans.
Strong field skills in wetland delineation and T&E assessments, including GPS data collection and ArcGIS/GIS applications.
Ability to identify wetlands, jurisdictional waters of the U.S., and associated soils, vegetation communities, wildlife species, and habitats common to the Intermountain West, Colorado, Utah, and Midwest regions.
Experience coordinating with federal, state, local, tribal, and regulatory agencies; Colorado permitting experience and familiarity with CDOT projects is preferred.
Professional certification as a Wetland Professional in Training (WPIT), Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS), or the ability to qualify for PWS certification is preferred.
Proven ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams, manage tasks and budgets, and deliver work on schedule.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and ArcGIS.

Annual Salary Range:
$52,000 - $90,000

Position Summary

The Drone Pilot / Surveyor is responsible for performing aerial data collection, mapping, surveying support, and construction documentation across utility-scale solar EPC projects. This position utilizes Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS), survey equipment, and specialized mapping software to collect accurate field data used to support engineering, estimating, construction, project controls, and site management.

Working within a fast-paced, self-perform EPC construction environment, the Drone Pilot / Surveyor will support projects throughout the construction lifecycle—from existing-condition and preconstruction surveys through earthwork, pile installation, electrical construction, progress tracking, quantity verification, and final project documentation.

The ideal candidate combines strong UAS flight capabilities with practical surveying and construction knowledge and understands how accurate, timely field data directly impacts the successful execution of large-scale solar projects.

Key Responsibilities

Plan and conduct UAS/drone flight operations across large utility-scale solar construction sites in accordance with FAA regulations, company procedures, and project requirements.
Collect high-resolution aerial imagery and survey data for mapping, topographic surveys, construction progress, inspections, and project documentation.
Perform photogrammetry and aerial mapping to produce Ortho mosaics, digital terrain models (DTMs), digital surface models (DSMs), point clouds, and other project deliverables.
Support site surveying activities utilizing GPS/GNSS, RTK, robotic total stations, and other survey equipment as required.
Establish, verify, and maintain survey control throughout the duration of construction.
Support construction layout and verification activities for roads, grading, drainage, equipment pads, pile locations, electrical infrastructure, substations, and other project components.
Perform existing-condition and preconstruction aerial surveys to document site conditions prior to mobilization and construction.
Conduct routine progress flights to document construction status and provide project teams with current aerial imagery.
Assist with earthwork quantity calculations, stockpile measurements, cut/fill analysis, and verification of completed work.
Support grading operations by providing accurate surface data and comparing existing conditions against design surfaces.
Provide survey and aerial data to support pile installation, tracker/racking construction, module installation, underground electrical systems, inverter/transformer locations, and other solar construction activities.
Compare collected field data against IFC drawings, design models, and project specifications to identify potential discrepancies.
Support quality control activities by documenting installed conditions and assisting with verification of completed construction.
Process and manage drone imagery and survey data using applicable photogrammetry, CAD, GIS, and mapping software.
Coordinate with Project Managers, Superintendents, Survey Managers, Engineers, Project Controls, and field personnel to determine survey and aerial data requirements.
Maintain accurate flight logs, survey records, field notes, control documentation, and project files.
Organize and maintain aerial imagery and survey data so information is readily accessible to project teams.
Identify potential site, design, or construction issues through review of aerial and survey data and communicate findings to project leadership.
Maintain UAS equipment, batteries, survey instruments, and associated technology in proper working condition.
Perform pre-flight inspections and evaluate weather, airspace, site conditions, and potential hazards prior to flight operations.
Ensure all UAS operations comply with FAA Part 107 requirements and applicable federal, state, local, client, and company requirements.
Coordinate flight activities with project safety and field leadership to ensure drone operations do not interfere with cranes, equipment, electrical work, or other construction activities.
Support multiple projects and travel between active construction sites based on project needs.

Required Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Surveying, Geomatics, Civil Engineering, Construction Management, GIS, or related technical discipline preferred.
Current FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate required.
Previous experience operating drones/UAS for surveying, mapping, engineering, or construction applications.
Working knowledge of surveying principles, coordinate systems, elevations, benchmarks, and construction layout.
Experience collecting and processing aerial imagery for photogrammetry and mapping applications.
Experience with GPS/GNSS and RTK survey equipment.
Ability to read and interpret civil plans, grading plans, site layouts, construction drawings, and specifications.
Understanding of survey control and the importance of horizontal and vertical accuracy in construction applications.
Strong computer and data-management skills.
Ability to work independently in large, active construction environments while coordinating effectively with field personnel.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.
Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to manage multiple assignments and priorities across multiple projects.
Valid driver's license and acceptable driving record.
Ability and willingness to travel extensively based on project requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience supporting utility-scale solar, renewable energy, heavy civil, power generation, or large-scale EPC construction projects.
Experience working for a self-perform EPC or heavy civil contractor.
Experience with DJI Enterprise, Trimble, Leica, Topcon, or similar professional UAS and survey equipment.
Experience with photogrammetry and mapping platforms such as Pix4D, DroneDeploy, Propeller, Trimble Business Center, or similar applications.
Working knowledge of AutoCAD, Civil 3D, GIS, or comparable design/mapping software.
Experience creating Ortho mosaics, point clouds, surface models, contour maps, and volumetric reports.
Experience performing cut/fill analysis and earthwork quantity verification.
Experience with Ground Control Points (GCPs), checkpoints, RTK/PPK workflows, and survey-grade drone mapping.
Familiarity with solar site grading, pile installation, tracker systems, access roads, drainage systems, underground electrical collection systems, substations, and related utility-scale solar construction.
Surveyor-in-Training (SIT/LSIT) certification or related surveying credentials are a plus but not required.

Ability to travel extensively and potentially remain near project sites for extended periods based on construction schedules.
Ability to work outdoors in varying weather and environmental conditions.
Ability to walk large utility-scale solar sites over rough and uneven terrain.
Ability to stand and walk for extended periods while performing field operations.
Ability to carry and set up drone, survey, GPS, and related field equipment.

Position Title

Job Description

Welcome to the Oregon Department of Forestry

Our Mission
– To protect and promote resilient forests that benefit all Oregonians.

The Benefits Of Joining Our Team

Work/life balance, 11 paid holidays a year, flexible work schedules, competitive benefits packages and so much more. Great Benefits Package - watch this video here. You’ll be part of the ODF team that serves our fellow Oregonians relying on regulation and protection of both public and private forest land in our great state of Oregon! Click here .

This position will be located at and report to the Salem office daily. The position will require work in the office, or field, full-time during the first month of employment and may be eligible for a hybrid/remote work schedule with the ability to report to Salem when business or operational needs are dependent on onsite activities . Occasional travel may be required.

What We Are Looking For

This position is part of the Water Quality and Monitoring Unit in the Forest Resources Division in Salem. The purpose of this division is to encourage economically efficient forest practices that ensure the continuous growing and harvesting of forest tree species, consistent with the sound management of soil, air, water, fish and wildlife resources and to assure the continued benefits of these resources for future generations; and to provide technical and financial assistance to non-federal forest landowners to improve management on private forest lands. The benefits derived from this program affect all Oregonians.

The Compliance Monitoring Program within the Forest Resources Division is responsible for monitoring the implementation of forest practice rules and analyzing compliance rates. The program collects information that allows for improvement in landowner compliance with the forest practices rules through training and education. Therefore, the compliance monitoring program works closely with the ODF Training Program to deliver presentations and other forms of communication to targeted audiences including landowners, operators, and ODF field foresters. Withing the compliance monitoring program, a team of Monitoring Specialists plan, implement, and report out on monitoring studies annually.

The Monitoring Specialist Duties Include

Plan, conduct, analyze, and report on forest monitoring projects statewide.
Perform extensive fieldwork, with some overnight travel, to collect environmental and forest practice data.
Manage, organize, and analyze complex datasets and GIS data using using ArcGIS Pro.
Train, lead, and oversee seasonal staff and/or work teams performing data collection.
Develop, coordinate, and oversee work completed by contractors, as assigned.
Interpret monitoring results and provide recommendations or, further study needs, to the Monitoring Coordinator and program managers.
Apply technical knowledge of the Forest Practices Act, DEQ water quality standards, and state and federal regulatory requirements to support program objectives.
Provide support to the Protection from Fire Program during wildfire or other emergency incidents.

Minimum Qualifications

Two years of experience in Forestry or a closely related natural resource field, and
a bachelor's degree in Forestry or a closely related natural resource field.

OR

Three Additional Years Of Related (pertinent) Experience

OR

One year of experience in Forestry or a closely related natural resource field and
a master's degree in Forestry or a closely related natural resource field.

Note:
Driver’s License Check - This position requires the operation of a state vehicle for the purpose of conducting official State business. If your license is from outside Oregon, you must submit at least a three-year court/DMV printout. If you have an Oregon driver’s license, a record check will be conducted on the top candidate to ensure a valid license and acceptable driving record.

Desired Skills

Proficiency with GIS tools and spatial data management
Field data collection skills across diverse forest resource topics
Ability to lead, train, and coordinate seasonal field crews
Strong data management, quality control, and database skills

Sicherstellung der EH&S-Compliance und regulatorischen Anforderungen, einschließlich gesetzlicher und behördlicher Berichte, Genehmigungen sowie Unterstützung im Austausch mit staatlichen und nichtstaatlichen Behörden und weiteren Stakeholdern.

Verantwortung für die Weiterentwicklung und Umsetzung eines ganzheitlichen Gesundheits- und Wellbeing-Managements im europäischen CSL Plasma Netzwerk unter Berücksichtigung globaler Vorgaben und lokaler gesetzlicher Anforderungen.

Position Summary

The Drone Pilot / Surveyor is responsible for performing aerial data collection, mapping, surveying support, and construction documentation across utility-scale solar EPC projects. This position utilizes Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS), survey equipment, and specialized mapping software to collect accurate field data used to support engineering, estimating, construction, project controls, and site management.

Working within a fast-paced, self-perform EPC construction environment, the Drone Pilot / Surveyor will support projects throughout the construction lifecycle—from existing-condition and preconstruction surveys through earthwork, pile installation, electrical construction, progress tracking, quantity verification, and final project documentation.

The ideal candidate combines strong UAS flight capabilities with practical surveying and construction knowledge and understands how accurate, timely field data directly impacts the successful execution of large-scale solar projects.

Key Responsibilities

Plan and conduct UAS/drone flight operations across large utility-scale solar construction sites in accordance with FAA regulations, company procedures, and project requirements.
Collect high-resolution aerial imagery and survey data for mapping, topographic surveys, construction progress, inspections, and project documentation.
Perform photogrammetry and aerial mapping to produce Ortho mosaics, digital terrain models (DTMs), digital surface models (DSMs), point clouds, and other project deliverables.
Support site surveying activities utilizing GPS/GNSS, RTK, robotic total stations, and other survey equipment as required.
Establish, verify, and maintain survey control throughout the duration of construction.
Support construction layout and verification activities for roads, grading, drainage, equipment pads, pile locations, electrical infrastructure, substations, and other project components.
Perform existing-condition and preconstruction aerial surveys to document site conditions prior to mobilization and construction.
Conduct routine progress flights to document construction status and provide project teams with current aerial imagery.
Assist with earthwork quantity calculations, stockpile measurements, cut/fill analysis, and verification of completed work.
Support grading operations by providing accurate surface data and comparing existing conditions against design surfaces.
Provide survey and aerial data to support pile installation, tracker/racking construction, module installation, underground electrical systems, inverter/transformer locations, and other solar construction activities.
Compare collected field data against IFC drawings, design models, and project specifications to identify potential discrepancies.
Support quality control activities by documenting installed conditions and assisting with verification of completed construction.

Maintain UAS equipment, batteries, survey instruments, and associated technology in proper working condition.
Perform pre-flight inspections and evaluate weather, airspace, site conditions, and potential hazards prior to flight operations.
Ensure all UAS operations comply with FAA Part 107 requirements and applicable federal, state, local, client, and company requirements.
Coordinate flight activities with project safety and field leadership to ensure drone operations do not interfere with cranes, equipment, electrical work, or other construction activities.
Support multiple projects and travel between active construction sites based on project needs.

Required Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Surveying, Geomatics, Civil Engineering, Construction Management, GIS, or related technical discipline preferred.

Previous experience operating drones/UAS for surveying, mapping, engineering, or construction applications.
Working knowledge of surveying principles, coordinate systems, elevations, benchmarks, and construction layout.
Experience collecting and processing aerial imagery for photogrammetry and mapping applications.
Experience with GPS/GNSS and RTK survey equipment.
Ability to read and interpret civil plans, grading plans, site layouts, construction drawings, and specifications.
Understanding of survey control and the importance of horizontal and vertical accuracy in construction applications.
Strong computer and data-management skills.

Previous experience supporting utility-scale solar, renewable energy, heavy civil, power generation, or large-scale EPC construction projects.
Experience working for a self-perform EPC or heavy civil contractor.
Experience with DJI Enterprise, Trimble, Leica, Topcon, or similar professional UAS and survey equipment.
